items.title: Step 1
items.description:
In this workshop, you will practice working with ARIA by building an accessible audio controller.

To start, add an `h1` element with the text `Audio Controls`.

hints.text: You should have an `h1` element.
Your `h1` element should be inside your `body` element.
Your `h1` element should have the text `Audio Controls`.

items.title: Step 2
items.description:
Next, add a `button` element with the `type` attribute set to the value `button`.

The `button` element's text should be `Play`.

hints.text: You should have a `button` element.
Your `button` element should have a `type` attribute.
Your `button` element should have the `type` attribute set to `button`.
Your `button` element should have the text `Play`.

items.title: Step 3
items.description:
Next, add a `div` element to contain all the elements for the volume control.

A `span` element is a generic inline container for content. It's commonly used to style a piece of text differently from the surrounding text, or to wrap text and give it an `id` that other elements (such as ARIA attributes) can reference.

Inside the `div` element, nest a `span` element with an `id` attribute set to `volume-label`.
Also, the text for the `span` element should be `Volume`.

The `id` will later be referenced by ARIA attributes so assistive technologies can identify this text as the label for the volume control.

hints.text: You should have a `div` element below your `button` element.
You should have a `span` element inside your `div` element.
Your `span` element should have an `id` attribute.
Your `span` element should have an `id` attribute with the value set to `volume-label`.
hints.test:
const spanEl = document.querySelector('button + div > span');
assert.equal(spanEl?.getAttribute('id'), 'volume-label');

hints.text: Your `span` element should have the text `Volume`.
hints.test:
const spanEl = document.querySelector('button + div > span');
assert.equal(spanEl?.innerText.trim(), 'Volume');

items.seed: Audio Controls

items.title: Step 4
items.description:
Now it is time to add another `span` element.

This `span` element should have an `id` attribute set to `volume-description`.
Also, the text for this `span` element should be `Adjust the sound level`.

Similar to the previous `span` element, the `id` of this `span` will later be referenced by ARIA attributes so assistive technologies can identify this text as the description for the volume control.

hints.text: You should have two `span` elements inside the `div` element.
Your second `span` element should have an `id` attribute.
Your second `span` element should have an `id` attribute with the value of `volume-description`.
Your second `span` element should have the text `Adjust the sound level`.
hints.test:
const secondSpanEl = document.querySelector('div > span:nth-of-type(2)');
assert.equal(secondSpanEl?.innerText.trim(), 'Adjust the sound level');

items.title: Step 5
items.description: Next, you need to add an `input` element with the `type` attribute set to `range` to create the volume slider. Set the `min` attribute to `0`, the `max` attribute to `100`, and the `value` attribute to `50` to define the default volume level.

hints.text: You should have an `input` element below your second `span` element.
hints.test:
const inputEl = document.querySelector('div > span:nth-of-type(2) + input');
assert.exists(inputEl);

hints.text: Your `input` element should have a `type` attribute.
Your `input` element should have a `type` attribute with the value `range`.
Your `input` element should have a `min` attribute.
Your `input` element should have a `min` attribute with the value `0`.
Your `input` element should have a `max` attribute.
Your `input` element should have a `max` attribute with the value `100`.
Your `input` element should have a `value` attribute.
Your `input` element should have a `value` attribute with the value `50`.

items.title: Step 6
items.description:
As you recall from prior lessons, the `aria-labelledby` attribute is used when there is existing text on the page that can be used as a label. In this case, you have added the `id` attribute to your `span` elements which will now be used here.

Add an `aria-labelledby` attribute to the `input` element set to `volume-label volume-description`.

hints.text: Your `input` element should have a `aria-labelledby` attribute.
Your `input` element should have a `aria-labelledby` attribute with the value `volume-label volume-description`.

items.title: Step 7
items.description:
Your accessible audio controller is almost complete but there is one last thing to add.

Add a `button` element with the `type` attribute set to `button` and with text `Mute` below the `div` element.

And with that change, you have completed this workshop!

hints.text: You should have a `button` element below the `div` element.
Your `button` element should have a `type` attribute.
Your `button` element should have a `type` attribute with the value `button`.
Your `button` element should have the text `Mute`.
